title: GSM8K: Training Verifiers for Grade-School Math
hook: Instead of trusting a model's first answer, sample many and let a learned 'verifier' pick the best — and it beats just finetuning, scaling better with data.
key_points: Introduces GSM8K, 8.5K high-quality, linguistically diverse grade-school math word problems.
Trains 'verifier' models to judge candidate solutions sampled from the model.
Ranks sampled solutions by verifier score and keeps the top one.
Verification beats a finetuning baseline and scales better with more data.
content_html: Karl Cobbe, Vineet Kosaraju, Mohammad Bavarian, and colleagues at OpenAI introduce GSM8K, a dataset of 8,500 high-quality, linguistically diverse grade-school math word problems, and use it to study a better way to get correct answers. Rather than relying on the model's single attempt, they train "verifier" models to judge candidate solutions, then rank many sampled solutions by verifier score. This verification approach significantly outperforms a finetuning baseline and scales better with data.
extra_html:
How it works

First, the model generates many candidate solutions to a problem. A separate verifier — trained to predict whether a solution is correct — scores each candidate, and the highest-scoring one is selected as the final answer. Compared with simply finetuning a model to produce a single solution, this sample-and-verify pipeline produces more correct answers, and its advantage grows as more training data is added, suggesting verification is a more data-efficient way to spend supervision.

Why it matters

GSM8K became a standard benchmark for arithmetic reasoning, popular precisely because grade-school problems are easy to state but require multi-step reasoning to solve. Beyond the dataset, the verifier idea was an early signal toward reward models for reasoning: instead of teaching a model to be right on the first try, you teach a separate model to recognize good reasoning and let it filter. That pattern echoes through later work on reasoning and reinforcement learning.
